reviews.review:
I played this a decent amount during the open testing and after beating it a couple times, thought it was fine enough. But after waiting a few months for a large update or two, it still feels off. The gunplay just feels very weak, and the upgrades and items you get just aren't very fun or creative. I forget monsters even get stronger in the dark honestly, because they just get beefier, that's really it. 

They heavily lean into this gimmick, but that's all it really is. A gimmick. Nothing wrong with gimmicks, but it doesn't really change how you play or approach them. You just shoot while slowly walking to the side so you don't die. Nothing your character does is particularly interesting or fun, and the gunplay feels so off. I wish I could explain it. Most games feel good from the jump, especially shooters, but this one doesn't. I think they need to take a step back and think about the core gameplay, because it just doesn't feel very varied or different. 

They can add as much content with characters and maps but the enemies and gameplay itself just aren't there, when they should be at this stage.
reviews.developer_response:
Thank you for your feedback.

We're constantly tweaking gun-play and mechanics of the game in this early access period. I hope that you'll come back again in the coming weeks and give the game another try!

reviews.review:
The combat formula is very interesting and well-executed as you not only have to focus on aiming and dealing damage but also on keeping the battlegrounds in the light in order to deal with the easy version of the enemies giving the combat an extra tactical level that makes for a fun core loop. It gets more interesting once you get items that boost the character in the shade or other types of items that turn the combat in new strategic directions. 

Combat is very responsive and you get clear feedback of the actions you take against the enemies, but feedback fails when enemies hit the player as they can deal a considerable amount of damage in a few seconds and the player only receive a too subtle screen effect. Also, the health bar doesn’t change as you lose hit points and it lacks a twinkl when the player is on the verge of dying.

Also, enemies out of camera frame can shoot and hit the player as any other in frame enemies, which leads to frustrating and unexpected death screens, as the game it’s also missing a directional damage indicator. These types of “cheats” help to sell a more streamlined experience where the player is not overwhelmed by the number of enemies the game can throw at you in quick succession.

Another aspect to improve the game is the tutorial to its systems, as right now, and understandably, the tutorial is a series of text and image screens. And a more easy and progressive approach to every aspect of the game and its enemies will make the first contact a more enjoyable experience since I got attacked in the first seconds of gameplay before I could test my Character, Camera, and Control. These are the type of things I have no doubt are in the production planning and will come out as the game comes out of early access.

The same will be with maps and activities, as right now, both maps I played felt pretty much the same, even if they were ambient at different times. Runs can feel repetitive between them since the game loop is so tightly planned that emergent gameplay can suffer even if the player has a choice on what activities it wishes to take on.

Some activities are definitely tougher than others. Reactor activation is significantly harder to get on 3 stars than the museum mission, even if I felt more overwhelmed in the latter. The bikini stealers one (I really liked the concept and made me laugh btw 10/10 pts) as much as I like it I never got feedback on how many could escape, or if I was doing good or bad.

As for level design, without upgrades, vertical navigation feels forced and sometimes difficult, and having to walk so much looking for the way up the mountains was tiresome. There is a dead-end in Waikiki Beach next to a road that felt wasted.

Some other quick bits:

The Play screen at first contact was weird as I had access to the upgrade store and challenges too. It could improve the experience if it was unlocked after fulfilling a milestone while playing so the player can ease up into the game.

Also, the challenges screen features the rewards, but no info on what the reward is, just the icon of some weapons and tools.

I also had a very tough time getting my health back, something typical of the rogue-like genre but nonetheless, it could be a crouch for bad players to get the know-how on what to do to farm some hp points in dire situations.

Some enemies trespass assets collisions, which can be funny at times.
reviews.developer_response:
Hey Rober,

Thanks for your very detailed feedback.
It's been circulated amongst the team, in particular around tutorials and balancing out some mission difficulty. 

We hope that you continue to enjoy the game, and look out for all the balancing, tweaks and additional content in the following months!
